what: The literature: what practitioners and researchers actually call the moves we make in copy, video and pictures. Every term with a plain definition, the field it comes from, the medium it applies to and how well it was checked. A term the controls already use is marked; the rest are names we had not used yet.
source: Researched 2026-10-23 on the owner's word ("research the actual naming conventions for creativity across these different domains ... put definitions to all of these things and get ones that I haven't even named"): Goldenberg, Mazursky & Solomon; Phillips & McQuarrie; Forceville; Smith & Yang; Pricken; McQuarrie & Mick; rhetoric; comedy craft; visual art and internet aesthetics; film and editing; platform craft; copywriting craft.

terms.what: An abstract, repeatable pattern that successful ads share; usable as an ideation recipe
Bring a symbol that carries the message into the product's space
The product, or one of its traits, replaces a symbol that already carries the message
Same as above but the symbol is pushed to an extreme instead of just transplanted
An unrealistic scenario that makes one product attribute impossible to miss
Show an unrealistic substitute doing the product's job, so the real product looks obviously better
The attribute, or the value of the product, is exaggerated to unrealistic size
Show what happens if you do, or do not, take the advised action
The consequence is pushed to an absurd size
Show the bad outcome of NOT using the product
Put the product in a contest with something from a different class that should beat it

terms.term: Attribute in competition / worth in competition
terms.what: The contest is about a product trait, or about whether the product is worth having
The contest is a surprising use of the product
Make the viewer do something with the medium so they feel the benefit
Viewer actually acts, or is asked to imagine acting
Change the product's dimension relative to its surroundings
Two unrelated parameters become linked (e.g. speed shown by shrinking an ocean)
Duplicate the product and compare the copies, or split it into parts and relate them
Jump the product across time to show a trait

terms.term: Later re-cut (2007-ish book): Unification, Activation, Metaphor, Subtraction, Extreme consequence, Absurd alternative, Inversion, Extreme effort, Attribute-value mapping
terms.what: A newer list of named templates from the same research line. Only the chapter names were seen
Two things shown side by side, equal weight
Two things merged into one object
One thing is absent; the viewer infers it from what stands in its place
The picture says "A goes with B" (association)
The picture says "A is like B"
The picture says "A is not like B"
Juxtaposition < fusion < replacement in how much the viewer must infer; authors predicted harder puzzles are liked and remembered more. A later test found only partial support

terms.term: Van Enschot et al. replacement subtype 1: source without target context
terms.what: The stand-in object appears alone with no cue from the product's world
The stand-in object sits inside the product's setting
The product appears inside the stand-in object's setting. Rated most fluent and pleasing in that study (secondary report)
The thing being described, the thing it is likened to, and the quality carried over
Target and source fused into one impossible object (e.g. a planet that is half candle)
Target is placed in a scene that makes you think of the absent source (a bottle in an ice bucket for sparkling wine)
Target and source both fully shown, linked by a shared visual trait (posture, colour, shape)
The target itself is posed or shaped so it evokes the source, with nothing else shown
Forceville maps contextual to P&M "replacement", simile to "juxtaposition", hybrid to "fusion". Warns that hybrid and integrated types alter the product and can look like damage
Metaphor carried by picture plus words together (1996 term)
How far an ad departs from the usual; the umbrella for the five factors below
How well the ad's unusual parts still connect to the message and the buyer. Creativity perception depends on divergence AND relevance together
Rare, surprising elements that move away from the obvious
Several ideas, or ideas that jump from one subject to another
Unexpected added detail; a basic idea built out into something more complex
Joining things normally unrelated
Pleasing language, colour or shape; craft
One study found professionals weight divergence more; consumers weight relevance, craftsmanship and humor more
Tell it entirely visually, no copy
Combine two unlike things

terms.term: Pricken: Comparative juxtaposition (2008 ed.: "compare and contrast")
terms.what: Set the product against something that makes the benefit obvious at a glance
Show the same thing many times so volume carries the point
Blow one trait up past believable
Invert the expected logic or roles
Leave out the key thing and let the viewer supply it
Impossible objects or tricks of seeing
Inspiring idea, brilliantly executed, fit for purpose; for crafts: is it brilliantly crafted and does craft lift the idea
Animation, casting, cinematography, direction, editing, illustration, photography, production design, sound design and use of music, typography, visual effects, plus writing
The stated main judging criterion for craft Lions is how well the idea is executed
A figure is a purposeful departure from what the audience expects, in a repeatable pattern
A figure built by arranging form: repetition (simple) or reversal (complex)
A figure that changes meaning: substitution (simple) or destabilization (complex)
Two different things pictured with a similar form so the eye links them
Two opposed things pictured in parallel
Picture says A is B; picture reads two ways at once

Ads with these figures drew more elaboration and a better attitude toward the ad, without being harder to understand. Visual figures worked even with casual exposure; verbal ones only when people were told to study
Metaphor and pun benefits faded for viewers lacking the cultural knowledge the ad assumed
Deliberate exaggeration for effect
Saying less than the truth; litotes does it by negating the opposite
Naming a thing by something attached to it
A part stands for the whole
Presenting the reverse of what is expected or meant
Opposites in parallel structure
Human traits on a non-human thing
One word governs several others, read differently each time
Contradiction inside a phrase or situation
Wordplay on multiple meanings
Question asked to persuade, not to get an answer
Same opening words repeated across phrases
A drop from high to low register for comic or deflating effect
The one unusual pattern a scene is built around; find it, then play it
The first moment that departs from normal; usually becomes the game
Raise the stakes or push the behavior to extremes, one beat at a time
Dig into why the character does it (psychology)

terms.term: "If this is true, then what else is true"
terms.what: A drill for heightening and exploring the game
Keep raising absurdity or stakes until tension forces a resolution; static characters kill the joke
Two items set a pattern, the third breaks it; also a rhythm rule in plain prose
Lead the listener down one path, then reveal the other
A joke that points back to an earlier joke in the same piece
A callback repeated again and again
A running gag whose first instance failed, dooming the rest (TV writers' slang)
The closing joke of a scene that earns the cut
An extra punchline stacked on the same setup
Set up a familiar expectation, deliver a different outcome
Joke form whose punchline is withheld or deliberately obvious; the letdown is the joke. Types: shaggy dog, obvious punchline, deliberately bad performance
Flat, expressionless delivery; the joke is the gap between calm delivery and ridiculous content
Laughs from social awkwardness; obliviousness of the character makes the audience squirm
A remark or action with no logical link to what came before
Comedy that deliberately breaks cause-and-effect; tools: juxtaposition, non sequitur, nonsense, subverted expectation
A different thing sharing the name: how people react to a meaningless world. Not a joke style
Characters constantly raise or lower their standing through words and body; comedy comes from status mismatches
Accept what a partner gives and add to it, instead of denying it
Named, numbered, odd detail beats generic; each detail must serve the surprise
A joke is an assumption set up, then violated
Dreamlike, illogical scenes; core tool is juxtaposition of distant realities
The farther apart the two joined realities, the stronger the image (Reverdy)
The impossible placed in a grounded world and treated as routine; contrast surrealism, which is inward/dream
Sharper, more detailed than a photo, often with narrative or emotion
Faithful copy of a photo; precise, usually unemotional
Realistic detail that fools the eye into seeing 3D on a flat surface
Show the ordinary in an unfamiliar way so habit-dulled perception wakes up
Everyday objects blown up (Oldenburg) or shrunk until they read as monuments
A picture of an object labeled as not the object; picture-vs-word contradiction
Mass-market sentimental style, sincere
Knowing, ironic love of artifice and excess; "naive" (accidental) vs "deliberate" camp (Sontag)
Almost-human or almost-right things provoke unease
"More is more": dense, layered, ornamented
"Less is more": reduced to essentials
Empty transitional places (corridors, waiting rooms) whose missing people feel eerie or nostalgic
A liminal-space fiction: endless empty yellow rooms
A photo that feels eerie because of its subject, poor quality, or both
Both blessed and cursed: funny and deeply uncomfortable at once
Image repeatedly filtered or recompressed: heavy distortion, oversaturation, compression artifacts
Deliberately bad, ironic, trolling-quality posting; compared to Dada's context-free nonsense
Memes built on layers of irony until odd and senseless; an escape from mainstream meme trends
Slang for low-quality compulsive short-form content; a 2025 meme genre of AI-generated absurd characters
Tag for a named aesthetic (cottagecore, normcore, corecore...)
Deliberately unpolished look: phone footage, plain text, rough sound
One image that reads two ways

terms.term: Shot scale (extreme long, long, full, medium long, medium, medium close-up, close-up, extreme close-up)
terms.what: How much of the subject fills the frame
Frame size reads as relationship: head-and-face intimate, waist-up personal, full figure social
Subject looks at the viewer (demand) or is displayed to be looked at (offer)
Low angle reads dominant, high angle reads smaller
Scene as a character sees it
Standard conversation framings
Camera rolled so horizon slants; unease, disorientation; heavy-handed if overused
Mean shot duration; short = urgent and fast, long = relaxed
Cut that removes the middle of one take so the subject leaps; abrupt, fast, calls attention to editing
Cut between shots lined up by action or subject so it flows
Match by shape, colour or movement, inviting comparison between two scenes. Video cousin of visual rhyme
Cut mid-movement to hide the edit
Pan so fast it smears; used as a transition or to signal time passing or chaos
Meaning comes from two shots side by side more than from either alone; the editing version of juxtaposition
Material that appears to be recorded by the characters: handheld, shaky, improvised, amateur look

terms.term: Lens and distance (wide lens exaggerates depth and distortion; telephoto compresses depth)
terms.what: How focal length and camera distance change the look and intimacy
Shake and drift read as amateur/real; steady reads produced
Looks and feels like what normally lives in that feed; made for the platform, not repurposed
Not overly polished; blends into the feed
Real creators, employees or customers on camera
Built on current sounds, memes or challenges
The opening seconds built to stop the scroll; TikTok says land it in 6 seconds
State the core message in the first 3 seconds
On-screen words per second (TikTok suggests about 5 to 10)
3-second plays divided by impressions
Share who keep watching past the hook; definition varies by tool (15-second, ThruPlay or full view over 3-second plays)
Opening beat that breaks the viewer's scroll rhythm; warning that an unconnected weird first frame buys curiosity but weak intent
Deliberately low-polish creative that does not read as an ad; a vendor report claims it is over-represented among top DTC ads
Low-production ad that looks like it came from a real customer or creator
Ad run through a creator's account
Performance drop when the audience has seen the same ad too often
The core creative idea (testimonial, demo, founder message)
The message bet (reason to buy); some sources treat it as the same as concept
The container: UGC video, studio, static, carousel
A small change to a concept (new hook, colour, opening clip)
Ad delivery now treats near-identical creatives as one; vendors say vary concept, hook, persona, format. No official similarity number exists
Add new creatives when results sag; keep a stockpile
Real figures and named particulars persuade; platitudes leave no impression
Research the product and give concrete reasons
Copy so smooth the reader cannot stop; first sentence exists to get the second read
Short teasers like "more on this later" that pull the reader on
24-item list incl. curiosity, specificity, simplicity, exclusivity, urgency, honesty, hope, guilt
Mail sorted over the bin: personal-looking survives, ad-looking is binned
Market hunger beats clever product
Unaware, problem aware, solution aware, product aware, most aware
How many claims the market has already heard; later levels need mechanism and proof
Aim copy at a desire people already hold

terms.term: Tone of voice, four axes (Nielsen Norman Group)
terms.what: Formal-casual, serious-funny, respectful-irreverent, matter-of-fact-enthusiastic; each a continuum
Words steer which meaning of an image you take
Words and picture each carry part of the story
Voice = steady personality; tone = mood for the moment; register = formality level of the language
Concrete scene and senses instead of stated claims
Write as to one specific person; Halbert's personal-envelope idea is the closest sourced cousin

terms.term: Intertextual devices in ads: quotation, allusion, parody, pastiche
terms.what: Borrowing from a known text or image; parody is humorous reinterpretation, pastiche is homage-style
Reuse an existing image or ad and change its meaning
Five humor types and three processes (incongruity-resolution, arousal-safety, disparagement). Category names not retrieved

terms.term: Executional frameworks (lecture vs drama, slice of life, demonstration, testimonial, fantasy)
terms.what: Textbook list of ways to present a message. The owner's "dramatisation" lives here
A scene built roughly in 3D before the real shoot or render, to lock camera, sizes, depth and light
The objects, surfaces and finishes placed in a set to say where and when the scene is
The whole designed world of a piece: sets, props, palette and signage working as one idea
The one object the camera and the story revolve around, built and lit with the most care
Words that exist inside the scene, on a sign, flag, label or screen, rather than laid over the picture
Creative tied to a season, holiday or live cultural moment, dressed in its look and colours
A planned set of colours for a scene or a moment, chosen for what they signal
Light whose direction and colour come from a source that exists in the scene (a window, a lamp), so it reads as real
